title: Revalidate mutable filesystem identity at publication boundaries
summary: Path validation alone is not filesystem authority when another process can mutate links or ancestors between check and use.
problem_pattern: Code validates a path, symlink state, link count or inode and then performs a consequential write or rename without binding the operation to stable descriptors and final identity checks.
failure_mode: TOCTOU races can redirect writes, mutate shared inodes or publish artifacts with unexpected links.
root_cause: Security relies on pathname re-resolution or a single pre-operation check across a mutable namespace.
prevention_rule: Use descriptor-relative no-follow traversal, avoid in-place mutation of untrusted existing inodes, and revalidate inode identity/link count immediately around publication with fail-closed cleanup.
preflight_checks: inspect ancestor traversal for pathname re-resolution
inspect overwrite behavior for mutation of old inodes
add deterministic race regressions, not only static bad-state tests
applicability_notes: Generic for artifact writers, caches, evidence files and any mutable filesystem namespace.
